extracted.intended_audience: public relations and corporate communications professionals; marketers; brand managers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for corporate advertising campaigns and the accompanying press releases, with emphasis on preventing and managing public backlash and crisis response. Focuses on pre-release vetting, messaging clarity, cultural sensitivity, and post-release corrective actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-release vetting / testing (focus-grouping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should think things through (or focus-group) the campaign before release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece criticizes Pepsi for 'seemingly not thinking something through (or focus-grouping it)' — implying that campaigns should be vetted with diverse audiences and scenario-tested to anticipate reactions and avoid obvious missteps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have holding statements ready
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare holding statements and immediate-response materials in advance of a rollout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes Pepsi 'certainly doesn’t seem it had holding statements ready.' Good crisis communications require pre-drafted, approved messages so the company can respond quickly rather than offering weak or delayed one-line defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural sensitivity and context awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid belittling or co-opting contemporary and historic social movements; be aware of historical parallels and potential offense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics said the ad 'belittled both contemporary protests, including those by Black Lives Matter, and historic ones, such as the civil rights marches' and resembled an iconic protest image. Communications should assess whether imagery or themes could trivialize serious issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and imagery implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider how casting, wardrobe, and visual sequences will be read across different audiences and historical contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ad showed a white model before a police line in a way 'eerily similar' to a photograph of an African-American protester; communicators must evaluate representation choices to avoid unintended and harmful associations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Message clarity — avoid vague subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the subject and purpose of the campaign are clear to audiences; avoid ambiguous or mixed signals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post notes 'The subject of the march is unclear,' which contributed to misinterpretation. Press releases and creative should clearly state intent and the issue being addressed so audiences aren't left to infer meaning that may offend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely, sincere apology and corrective action
rubrics_metrics.description: When a campaign misfires, respond quickly with a sincere apology and take decisive corrective steps (e.g., remove content, halt rollout).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pepsi ultimately tweeted an apology and 'removing the content and halting any further rollout.' The article implies this is the appropriate follow-up to missed messaging — better done promptly and with empathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust internal review and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain rigorous internal approval processes so that multiple decision-makers responsibly vet campaigns before launch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author laments 'the amount of people who greenlit that advertisement,' highlighting the need for clear accountability and critical review rather than groupthink or rubber-stamping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive crisis planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning is essential: anticipate potential crises and build response plans into campaign development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The closing line, 'planning is the essence of crisis communications,' underscores that proactive planning (not just reactive statements) helps prevent and mitigate fallout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid tone-deafness; anticipate audience perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the campaign may be perceived as tone-deaf by various constituencies and evaluate from multiple vantage points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media criticized the ad as 'tone-deaf' and 'co-opting the resistance.' Teams should assess potential interpretations across demographics, activists, and media to avoid appearing insensitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor media and social reaction; expect rapid amplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Be prepared for immediate and widespread social and press reaction; monitor outlets and platforms closely during rollout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post cites rapid critical coverage (Washington Post, Adweek, Twitter), indicating campaigns can be 'clobbered in social' quickly — active monitoring enables faster, better-informed responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor content and rollout to formats and channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider how different versions and channels (e.g., 2-minute vs. 30-second, TV vs. digital) will be perceived and the different risks each carries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes the spot was released in '2-minute-plus and 30-second versions' across TV and digital; communicators should review each format's potential impact and ensure consistency of intent and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess celebrity/influencer involvement for reputational risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether using a celebrity might expose them or the brand to undue reputational harm or put individuals 'in this position.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pepsi 'apologize[d] for putting Kendall Jenner in this position.' Brands should weigh the risks to both the brand and the talent when involving high-profile figures in sensitive themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use press releases to clearly explain campaign intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Accompany creative with a press release that explicitly communicates the campaign's purpose, scope, and messaging to reduce misinterpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece references Pepsi's April 4 press release describing the ad as part of 'Live for Now' and its intended themes; however the release did not prevent backlash, suggesting releases should be clear, specific, and anticipate likely critiques.
